derivations.solution: Write \(3^{98}-3^{89}=3^{89}\left(3^{9}-1\right)\). Unit digits of powers of \(3\) repeat as \(3,9,7,1\), and both \(89\) and \(9\) leave remainder \(1\) on division by \(4\), so each of \(3^{89}\) and \(3^{9}\) ends in \(3\). Thus \(3^{9}-1\) ends in \(2\), and the product ends in the unit digit of \(3\times 2\), namely \(6\).

derivations.solution: Let the numbers be \(n,n+1,n+2,n+3\). Then the sum of squares is \(4n^{2}+12n+14=294\), which reduces to \(n^{2}+3n-70=0\), i.e. \((n-7)(n+10)=0\). Taking the natural solution \(n=7\), the numbers are \(7,8,9,10\). Their sum is \(34\).

derivations.reasoning: Sum of roots p + q = -p gives q = -2p; product pq = q with q nonzero gives p = 1, hence q = -2. Sympy returns the two solutions (0,0) and (1,-2), and q != 0 rules out the first. Check: x^2 + x - 2 = (x+2)(x-1) has roots 1 and -2, which are p and q.
derivations.solution: For \(x^{2}+px+q=0\) the sum of the roots is \(-p\) and the product is \(q\). Since the roots are \(p\) and \(q\), we need \(p+q=-p\) and \(pq=q\). As \(q\neq 0\), the second gives \(p=1\), and then the first gives \(q=-2\); indeed \(x^{2}+x-2=(x-1)(x+2)\) has roots \(1\) and \(-2\).

derivations.solution: Factorise as \((a-b)(a+b)=35\). The factor pairs are \(1\times 35\) and \(5\times 7\), giving \(a-b=1,\ a+b=35\) so \((a,b)=(18,17)\), and \(a-b=5,\ a+b=7\) so \((a,b)=(6,1)\). Hence there are exactly \(2\) such pairs.

derivations.solution: Putting \(x=b-6\) into \(x^{2}-6x+b=0\) gives \((b-6)^{2}-6(b-6)+b=0\), which simplifies to \(b^{2}-17b+72=0\). Factorising, \((b-8)(b-9)=0\), so \(b=8\) or \(b=9\); both work, since \(x^{2}-6x+8\) has root \(2=b-6\) and \(x^{2}-6x+9\) has root \(3=b-6\). The largest value of \(b^{2}\) is therefore \(81\).

derivations.solution: Completing the square, \(x^{2}+5x+10=\left(x+\frac{5}{2}\right)^{2}+\frac{15}{4}\), which is always positive with least value \(\frac{15}{4}\). The reciprocal of a positive quantity is largest when that quantity is smallest. Hence the maximum is \(\frac{4}{15}\).

derivations.solution: Work done is proportional to workers multiplied by days, so \(\frac{(x+2)(x-3)}{(x+4)(x-2)}=\frac{3}{4}\). Cross-multiplying, \(4x^{2}-4x-24=3x^{2}+6x-24\), which reduces to \(x^{2}-10x=0\). The root \(x=0\) is rejected because the numbers of days must be positive, leaving \(x=10\).

derivations.value: the claim that an even product forces both factors to be even
derivations.reasoning: The other three statements are true: 1 is a unit, neither prime nor composite; 0 is neither positive nor negative; sqrt2 is irrational. The claim that pq even forces both p and q even is false, since 2 x 3 = 6 is even with 3 odd; only ONE factor need be even.
derivations.solution: It is true that \(1\) is neither prime nor composite, that \(0\) is neither positive nor negative, and that \(\sqrt{2}\) is irrational. However, a product is even as soon as just one factor is even: \(2\times 3=6\) is even although \(3\) is odd. So the statement that an even product forces both numbers to be even is the incorrect one.

derivations.reasoning: Completing the square, 4(n^2 + 19n + 92) = (2n+19)^2 + 7, so if the value is k^2 then (2k)^2 - (2n+19)^2 = 7, i.e. (2k - m)(2k + m) = 7 with m = 2n + 19. The factorisations of 7 give m = +/-3, so 2n + 19 = 3 or -3, i.e. n = -8 or n = -11. A search over -2000 to 2000 confirms exactly these two, and both give the value 4. Their sum is -19.
derivations.solution: Multiplying by \(4\) and completing the square, \(4(n^{2}+19n+92)=(2n+19)^{2}+7\). So if \(n^{2}+19n+92=k^{2}\) then \((2k)^{2}-(2n+19)^{2}=7\), and since \(7\) is prime the only possibilities give \(2n+19=\pm 3\). Hence \(n=-8\) or \(n=-11\), each making the expression equal \(4\), and their sum is \(-19\).

derivations.solution: Factorising each: \(x^{3}+3x^{2}+3x+1=(x+1)^{3}\); \(x^{3}+5x^{2}+5x+4=(x+4)(x^{2}+x+1)\), since \(x=-4\) is a root; and \(x^{2}+5x+4=(x+1)(x+4)\). The LCM takes the highest power of every distinct factor. That gives \((x+1)^{3}(x+4)(x^{2}+x+1)\).

derivations.solution: The three brackets satisfy \((x-y)+(y-z)+(z-x)=0\), and whenever \(a+b+c=0\) we have \(a^{3}+b^{3}+c^{3}=3abc\). So the numerator equals \(3(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\). Dividing by \(9(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\) leaves \(\frac{3}{9}=\frac{1}{3}\).

derivations.reasoning: X = {a, {b}, c} and Y = {{a}, b, c} share only the element c, since a is not in Y ({a} is a different object) and {b} is not in Y. So X n Y = {c}. But Z = {a, b, {c}} contains {c}, not c, so ({c}) n Z is empty. Note option C, {Phi}, is a set containing the empty set and is therefore non-empty, so it is not the same thing.
derivations.solution: The only common element of \(X\) and \(Y\) is \(c\): the element \(a\) of \(X\) is not in \(Y\) (which contains the set \(\{a\}\), a different object), and \(\{b\}\) is not in \(Y\) either. So \(X\cap Y=\{c\}\). Now \(Z\) contains \(\{c\}\) but not \(c\) itself, so intersecting again leaves nothing, giving \(\Phi\). Note that \(\{\Phi\}\) would be a set with one element and so is not the same as the empty set.

derivations.reasoning: For px^2 + 3x + 2q = 0 the sum of the roots is -3/p and the product is 2q/p. Setting both equal to -6 gives p = 1/2 and 2q = -6p = -3, so q = -3/2. Then p - q = 1/2 + 3/2 = 2. Check with sympy: the roots of (1/2)x^2 + 3x - 3 are -3 +/- sqrt15, whose sum is -6 and product is -6.
derivations.solution: For \(px^{2}+3x+2q=0\), the sum of the roots is \(-\frac{3}{p}\) and the product is \(\frac{2q}{p}\). Setting \(-\frac{3}{p}=-6\) gives \(p=\frac{1}{2}\), and then \(\frac{2q}{p}=-6\) gives \(2q=-3\), so \(q=-\frac{3}{2}\). Hence \(p-q=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{3}{2}=2\).
